sources.title: Ernst Hairer and Gerhard Wanner, Introduction à l’Analyse Numérique, Chapter III: Équations Différentielles Ordinaires, University of Geneva course notes revised for 2004/05
sources.locator: §§III.2–III.5, PDF pp. 4–11 / printed pp. 60–67. In particular, §III.3 Theorem 3.1 and its full proof, PDF pp. 7–9 / printed pp. 63–65.
sources.reading_verification: The exact 30-page author-hosted PDF is cached under scratchpad/numerical-analysis-2026-10-12/sources/ode/ with SHA-256 71cc972bcacf4d24fba68f47e3da55b30a55ede0baf7e5f330168fb347db5236, matching the prior source dossier. I read the full relevant PDF range pp. 4–11, rendered pp. 7–9 to inspect the formulas, and checked Theorem 3.1's hypotheses, propagated-error estimate, local-error accumulation, and neighborhood-retention qualification. Theorem 3.1 assumes a uniform local defect and Lipschitz increment map; it does not certify an adaptive controller or a multistep method.

contents.name: III.2: Runge–Kutta one-step method, local error order, and method definition
contents.support: Supplies the exact local-defect convention and one-step-method setting. The local theorem in this batch states the map, domain, tube, and defect hypotheses explicitly; it does not infer a method order from a label.

contents.name: III.3: global convergence from local defect and step-map stability
contents.locator: §III.3, PDF pp. 7–9 / printed pp. 63–65, Theorem 3.1, equations (3.1)–(3.8), and complete proof
contents.support: Supports propagation and accumulation of the local errors. The local proof writes the finite geometric recurrence explicitly and adds the nonzero initial-error and L=0 branches.

contents.name: III.4: embedded Runge–Kutta estimates and step-size controller
contents.reason: The assigned items prove fixed-grid error bounds; they do not assert that an embedded difference or adaptive controller certifies a global error.

contents.name: III.5: multistep method definitions and Adams methods
contents.reason: No multistep method is analyzed or given an error guarantee in this pair.

sources.title: Tobias Embree, Lecture Notes on Numerical Analysis, Virginia Tech
sources.locator: Lecture 33, PDF p. 189, Euler truncation error; Lecture 34, §5.3, PDF pp. 190–192, explicit one-step global error analysis and complete geometric-series estimate (5.3).
sources.reading_verification: The complete 236-page PDF was opened. I read the full relevant pages 189–192, including the exact Euler local truncation calculation, the one-step error recurrence, the finite geometric sum, and the fixed-final-time order conclusion. The notes give a scalar formulation; this batch proves the vector-norm version directly rather than importing a scalar conclusion.

contents.name: Euler local truncation error and one-step global recurrence
contents.locator: Lecture 33, PDF p. 189; Lecture 34, §5.3, PDF pp. 190–192, equation (5.3)
contents.support: Independently confirms that local error and Lipschitz stability enter different terms of the recurrence, and that an O(h^p) one-step truncation error yields fixed-time O(h^p) global error.

contents.name: Adaptive Runge–Kutta step selection
contents.reason: The pair does not claim that an adaptive error estimate or tolerance alone is a global certificate.

sources.reading_verification: The complete 19-page arXiv v6 PDF was opened. I read the continuous normalizing flow theorem and the full Appendix A argument: the infinitesimal flow map, change-of-variables identity, Jacobi determinant differentiation, and trace limit. The source's theorem is used only for the density-evolution interface; it supplies no global discretization error theorem, and the local item states stronger C¹ flow and positive-density hypotheses.

sources.reading_verification: The complete 64-page JMLR PDF was opened. I read the full continuous-time flow definition, inverse-flow discussion, log-density integral, augmented state equation, and Euler discretization discussion in §§4.1–4.2.1. The paper presents solver-based computation and a local Euler expansion but no generic global state/log-density error theorem; this batch supplies that proof separately.
